pr_title: ESQL: Fix equals hashCode for functions
pr_body:
Fix https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104393.

For any descendants of `EsqlConfigurationFunction`, the `hashCode` and `equals` methods did not take the actual configuration into account. It is important that they do, since functions like `NOW` provide different results depending on the configuration; in particular, the actual `now` datetime is contained in the `EsqlConfiguration`.

Also, clean redundant implementations of `hashCode` and `equals` in other functions, whenever the inherited methods could just be used.
I went over all inheritors of `EsqlScalarFunction` for this.
pr_comments: Hi @alex-spies, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: ESQL: missing equals and hashCode for some functions
issue_context.body:
Some functions are missing correct implementations for `equals` and `hashCode`. This applies at least to
- ~~[DateDiff](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/scalar/date/DateDiff.java)~~ **Update:** This one is actually fine.
- [DateExtract](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/function/scalar/date/DateExtract.java) and other `ConfigurationFunctions` (we could just implement this for `ConfigurationFunction` in this case).

Other functions may need to be checked as well.
comments: Interesting that this hasn't bit us. I know we have a ton of function test case utilities, but they don't actually use equals and hashCode - they are more about building the function and running it.

review_comments: @not-napoleon maybe we should (separately to this PR) add test cases for functions that rely on the `EsqlConfig`. E.g. `NOW` actually derives its value from the config, which maybe could use a nice randomized test.

That's a good point.  Let's get a ticket open for that, so we don't forget.  for `NOW` at least, it might make sense for it to not use `AbstractFunctionTestCase` at all, since it doesn't really have any parameters we need to randomize, null, type check, etc.

The config was _always_ important for serialization and subsequent deserialization to produce equal results; now our csv tests actually catch this: without using the correct `EsqlConfiguration`, differences are being detected in e.g. `date_format` (and rightly so).
The implementation in `Function` also hashes the class name, likely causing fewer collisions.
Redundant, the implementation in `Function` already checks equality based on the children (all of the expressions).
